title: Multi-objective evolutionary feature selection on high-dimensional biological data, with a knockoff baseline
description: A budget-matched, nested-cross-validated comparison of NSGA-II and NSGA-III feature selection against random subsets, filter and embedded baselines, a model-X knockoff filter, and an oracle with access to the true support. The evolutionary search dominates random sampling on the inner-CV Pareto front and shows no statistically detectable advantage on held-out error, recovering none of the planted informative features where a t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction recovers seven of ten at a thousandth of the evaluation cost. Reported with Friedman ranks, Holm-corrected pairwise Wilcoxon tests, Cliff's delta and hypervolume against a fixed reference point.
